storyCards.headline: Space Oddity: A Cultural Moment Captured on Record
storyCards.fact:
David Bowie's "Space Oddity" reached #15 on the Billboard Hot 100. "Space Oddity" is a song by the English singer-songwriter David Bowie.

It was first released on 11 July 1969 by Philips and Mercury Records as a 7-inch single, then as the opening track of his second studio album, David Bowie.

Produced by Gus Dudgeon and recorded at Trident Studios in London, it is a tale about a fictional astronaut named Major Tom; its title and subject matter were partly inspired by the film 2001: A Space Odyssey (1968) and Bowie's feelings of alienation at that point in his career.

The song peaked at #15 on the Billboard Hot 100 and spent 15 weeks on the chart.

Chart story — peaked at #15 on the Hot 100.
